newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums end steady to touch firmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums end steady to touch firmer.

text.p: NWE gas oil was perkier on Monday with cargo premiums strong and IPE futures higher. Only barge premiums lost ground.
April IPE gas oil closed $1.25 higher at $170.75.

Heating oil barge premiums were pressured lower by a lack of demand, losing 75 cents or so. A barge was concluded at April IPE -$1 fob ARA for second half March. Traders said activity had been lacklustre.
The cargo market saw steady to firmer premiums amid concern about the amount of Russian gas oil that may be headed to the Far East.
With upwards of 500,000 tonnes looking to head to the strong Asian market the worry is of a depleted European market.
Russian cargoes themselves were showing steady premiums of April IPE +$2-3 cif ARA rather than gains, because of the difficulty in securing material.
"Most of it already has homes," said one trader.

DIN and FOD were benefitting from the potential for a squeezed European market with DIN attracting bids of around April IPE +$6-7 cif Germany. FOD narrowed the differential to DIN by moving up to around April IPE +$4 cif NWE.
However, the market was essentially restricted to talk rather than trade.
Diesel premiums were edging down as the market headed towards summer spec cargoes. Premiums were assessed at April IPE +$11-13 cif NWE.
"There is some support here because there are not overflowing supplies," said one trader.
